claims.text: The workflow audit is free, written, sent by email, and capped at one page. There are no calls.

sources.ref: Proposed format; Chris has not yet confirmed what his map contains

claims.text: This example is illustrative. It uses the booking-to-payment process from the CDCS Contracts demo, not a real client's business.

The CDCS demo has a booking form with a postcode distance check (free within 15 miles), review by email, a calendar file once dates are agreed, a private invoice link with CIS deducted, card payment through Stripe in test mode, a payment check before an invoice is marked paid, and a worker that resends failed notifications every 15 minutes.
In the demo, the owner still approves each job by email: approve, propose other dates, or decline.
If a tool is worth building, the next step is a written scope with a fixed price, agreed before any work starts.

sources.ref: chrisdemetriou-PMO Decision Log, 19 Oct 2026 (fixed price per agreed scope)

claims.text: The audit says plainly whether a custom tool is worth it.

sources.ref: https://chrisdemetriou.com/#contact ('tell you straight whether a custom tool is worth it'), approved by Chris 19 Oct 2026

body.text: One page, by email: each step of your process, who does it today, and which steps a tool could run. Below is an example, worked through on the booking-to-payment process from the CDCS Contracts demo. It is illustrative, not a real client.

body.heading: The steps a tool could run
body.text: In the CDCS demo, these steps run by themselves:
items: A contractor picks dates on a booking form, which checks the distance to the site by postcode (free within 15 miles).
Once dates are agreed, the contractor gets a calendar file automatically.
The invoice goes out as a private link, with CIS deducted, and the contractor pays by card through Stripe.
The payment is checked with Stripe before the invoice is marked paid.
If a notification fails, it is resent every 15 minutes until it goes through.

body.heading: The step that stays with a person
body.text: Deciding which jobs to take. In the demo, the owner approves each booking by email, proposes other dates, or declines. A good map is as clear about what should stay human as about what can be automated.

body.heading: What happens after the map
body.text: If a tool is worth building, you get a written scope with a fixed price, agreed before any work starts. If it isn't worth it, the map says so.
